narrative: Material PL3__M33A264B exhibits intermittent demand with mean daily demand of 2.66 units and CV of 1.80. Lead time averages 1.32 days with moderate variability (CV=0.96). The recommended safety stock is 11 units to achieve 95% service level, with reorder point at 15 units. Order quantity is set to 526 units, constrained by MOQ of 526; storage capacity of 1,499.79 units is not binding. Demand variability is the dominant factor in safety stock requirement.

research_insights.selected_model: Continuous-review (r,Q) model with Normal approximation safety stock
research_insights.selection_rationale: Intermittent demand with CV=1.80 and a binding MOQ of 526 units makes a fixed-order-quantity (r,Q) policy optimal. The Normal approximation for sigma_LTD is conservative for stuttering-Poisson demand, providing a buffer against distribution misspecification. EOQ falls below MOQ so the MOQ governs the order cycle.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Moderate — MOQ of 526 units results in a long ~198-day replenishment cycle relative to low daily demand. Any demand surge or lead-time extension during this cycle could erode the 11-unit safety stock rapidly. Storage capacity is non-binding (537 of 1,500 units used post-replenishment).
